title: Election Deniers Think the GOP’s Terrible Midterm Polling Is a ‘Psyop’
gist: Election deniers and Trump are branding the GOP's poor midterm polling a psyop to depress turnout; Trump has called polls fake 39 times while Reuters reports GOP money flowing to formerly safe races.

insights.claim: Election deniers, following Donald Trump's lead, are dismissing the GOP's poor midterm polling as fake, a psyop, or a ploy to suppress Republican turnout in November.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Signals a pre-emptive delegitimization of unfavorable midterm results and polling.

insights.claim: Heritage Foundation president Kevin Roberts told Fox News that midterm polling is a psyop meant to depress conservative turnout, showing the narrative has reached establishment conservative institutions.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Mainstream think-tank adoption widens the reach of the polling-denial narrative.

insights.claim: Steve Bannon called the recent polling a psyop and urged supporters that their fate remains in their own hands regardless of what media say about a blue wave.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Turnout-mobilization framing suggests the right is bracing for a Democratic wave narrative.
insights.quote: our fate is still in our hands

insights.claim: Seth Keshel branded negative polls a psyop and said polling is so unethical it should be outlawed, an escalation from distrusting polls to calling for their prohibition.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Watch for any policy or regulatory push against pollsters.
insights.quote: Polling is so unethical now it should be outlawed.

insights.claim: Trump has called polls fake 39 times since returning to the White House last year, nine of them in August alone, per Media Matters for America.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Rising frequency indicates the message is being intensified as the midterms approach.
insights.locator: Trump has called polls fake 39 times

insights.claim: Trump claimed on Truth Social that polls are Democratic 'demoralization operations' meant to stop Republicans voting, and told reporters 'The polls are fake' after negative Iowa polling.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Shows the president personally seeds the narrative that followers repeat.

insights.claim: Multiple polls show Trump's approval at historic lows with Democrats leading Senate races in states Trump won easily in 2024, and Reuters reported Republicans are spending in dozens of races they considered safe.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Defensive GOP spending points to a wider Senate map and possible House and Senate losses; relevant to policy-risk positioning.

insights.claim: Trump's own aides are reportedly extremely worried about losing both the House and Senate, with one operative telling WIRED the party will get creamed.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Private pessimism contrasts with public denial of polls.
insights.quote: Oh, yeah, we're going to get creamed,

insights.claim: Hundreds of GOP candidates for federal and statewide office in November have expressed doubts about the integrity of US elections, making election denial central to Republican belief.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Raises the odds of contested-result disputes after November.
insights.locator: For over a decade, Trump has claimed

insights.claim: Some MAGA figures concede weak polling reflects high gas prices and the ongoing war in Iran, but when Tim Pool said so Bill Mitchell replied that maybe the polls are fake, showing the narrative overrides economic explanations.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Gas prices and the Iran war are named drivers of Trump's weak approval, a macro headwind to watch.

insights.claim: Gunther Eagleman claimed he has never been polled and that polls are fake, yet a top commenter noted he repeatedly shares polls favorable to Trump, illustrating selective trust in polling.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Illustrates that the narrative is motivated rather than methodological.
insights.quote: Gunther LOVES polls when they are in his favor.

insights.claim: The Maryland Election Integrity Group claimed without evidence that polling has been skewed toward Democrats by three points on average over the last five cycles, a quantified but unsupported bias claim.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Unsupported; useful as an example of how poll-bias claims are being packaged.
